title: Challenge: SSH local port forward
intro: Scenario: a MySQL database runs on bastion host example.com and only listens on its own localhost:3306. A firewall blocks 3306 from the outside. Reach it from your laptop using an SSH local port forward. Type commands below; 'help' shows a hint, 'reset' starts over.

steps.instruction: Confirm you cannot reach the database directly yet. Try a client against your local port 3306.
steps.success: ERROR 2003 (HY000): Can't connect to MySQL server on '127.0.0.1:3306' (111 Connection refused)
steps.fail: Use a client (mysql / nc / telnet) pointed at port 3306 to prove it's unreachable.

steps.instruction: Open a local port forward: bind local 3306 to localhost:3306 on example.com, and don't open a remote shell.
steps.success: Tunnel established: localhost:3306 -> example.com -> localhost:3306. (no shell; running in foreground)
steps.fail: You need ssh with -L LOCAL:HOST:PORT to user@example.com. Add -N so no remote shell is opened.

steps.instruction: Leave the tunnel running. In a new shell, connect to the database through your local port 3306.
steps.success:
Welcome to the MySQL monitor.  Server version: 8.0.36
Connected through the SSH tunnel, the firewall never saw your traffic.
steps.fail: Same client command as step 1, now it succeeds because the tunnel forwards your local 3306 to the remote database.

done: Solved! You forwarded a firewalled remote service to your laptop with `ssh -N -L 3306:localhost:3306 user@example.com`.
